title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: Elastic Cloud
providers.scope_notes: Covers Elastic Cloud (Elastic Cloud Hosted / Serverless, Elasticsearch). Covers Elastic Cloud org API keys and Elasticsearch-level credentials on ECH, Serverless and self-managed; Elasticsearch audit logging needs a qualifying subscription, and the org-level Cloud audit trail exists only on FedRAMP Moderate.

controls.name: IP filters (network security policies)
controls.what: Rejects deployment/project traffic from non-allowed IPs with 403.
controls.setting: Organization > Network security > IP filter; apply to deployments

no_control.what: Service tokens cannot be given an expiry.
Built-in service accounts cannot be disabled.

controls_unknown: IP restriction for the Elastic Cloud API (api.elastic-cloud.com) used with Cloud API keys.
Whether an org can block creation of Cloud API keys with no expiry (Never).
Org-level audit log of Cloud API key creation/use outside FedRAMP Moderate.
Whether ES API keys owned by a SAML user stop working when the user is removed in the IdP.
Whether xpack.security.authc.api_key.enabled can be set in ECH user settings.
Whether Cloud API key revocation affects in-flight requests.

authentication.summary: Bearer token for a service account (e.g. elastic/fleet-server, elastic/kibana) with fixed privileges.

federation.details: Service-only credential, not usable by people.

ip_restriction.boundary: Only via deployment IP filters / HTTP filters; not per token.

renewal.summary: Create new token and delete old one.

administration.summary: manage_service_account for built-in accounts; manage_security for user-managed accounts. Built-in accounts are always enabled.
administration.conditions: User-managed service accounts appear in current API reference with an enabled flag.

offboard.details: Service accounts are for external services, not individual users.

inventory.details: Get service accounts API, then get service account credentials API per account (includes file-backed tokens).

usage.ui: Enable audit logging (xpack.security.audit.enabled: true); filter authentication.token.name

reads.ui: Audit log: filter access_granted and authentication.token.name

token_format.notes: Bearer token; secret part at least 22 chars.

anomaly_cues: Service token used from outside Fleet/Kibana hosts

containment.steps: Delete the token via API; file-backed tokens need the service_tokens file edited.
containment.notes: Index-backed token cache clears automatically when the security index changes (for example, a token delete); file-backed cache clears on file change. No derived tokens.

calls.reveals: Documents in indices covered by the service account's fixed privileges
calls.log_notes: Elasticsearch audit log (access_granted is in the default include list once auditing is enabled); needs a qualifying subscription. Token identified by authentication.token.name.

evidence.title: Elasticsearch API (OpenAPI) - Create a cross-cluster API key
Stack monitoring on ECH and ECE
Manage IP filters in ECH or Serverless
